commitResults.messageBody:
Alzara.java mixed command-handling logic with direct System.out/Scanner
calls in every switch case, making it hard to see the control flow and
impossible to reuse or swap the interaction layer independently.

Move all printing and input-reading into a new Ui class with named
methods (showWelcome, showTaskAdded, showError, readCommand, etc.).
Alzara.java now only orchestrates commands and talks to the user
through Ui, matching the target design's separation of concerns.

No behavioural change: the "task added" messages for todo/deadline/
event share one showTaskAdded(flavourText, task, taskCount) method
since they follow an identical shape, avoiding three near-duplicate
methods. Verified via the full UI regression suite (test-ui skill) -
all 9 test cases pass unchanged.

commitResults.messageTitle: Extract TaskList class to encapsulate the task list
commitResults.messageBody:
Alzara.java held the task list as a raw ArrayList<Task> that
every command case reached into directly.

Add a TaskList class wrapping the ArrayList and exposing add, get,
delete, and size as named operations. Storage.save and Ui.showTaskList still take a plain ArrayList<Task>, so TaskList exposes getTasks() for those two call sites

commitResults.messageTitle: Extract CommandParser class to parse command arguments
commitResults.messageBody:
Add a CommandParser class with parseTodo, parseDeadline, parseEvent,
and parseTaskIndex, each turning a raw command string into a Task (or
index) and throwing AlzaraException when the input is malformed.
Alzara.java's switch cases shrink to a few lines each that just call
the matching parse method and act on the result

Introduce a Command hierarchy for every user command
commitResults.messageBody:
Alzara's switch statement mixed checking the command with executing it in
every case.

Add an abstract Command class and one concrete
subclass per case: ExitCommand, AddCommand, MarkCommand, UnmarkCommand, DeleteCommand, ListCommand, and UnknownCommand

Unrecognised input was added to the task list as a raw Task via
UnknownCommand but never included a type letter (T/D/E), so
Storage.loadTask() could never parse them back, displaying an error
each time the tasks were loaded.

Remove the ability to add a task without a real command.

commitResults.messageBody:
find currently accepts only one keyword.

Let's change Task.matches and FindCommand to take String...
keywords instead of a single String. A
task now matches only if its description contains every one of the
given keywords, not just one.

commitResults.messageTitle: Merge branch 'branch-A-Varargs'
Document key assumptions with Java assertions
commitResults.messageBody:
TaskList.get()/delete() rely on callers to bounds-check the index
before calling while CommandParser's parseTodo/parseDeadline/parseEvent
slice the command text at fixed offsets that only work if the
command carries the expected keyword prefix. Neither assumption is
checked in code, so a caller that got either one wrong would fail
with a bare IndexOutOfBoundsException or a silently wrong
substring, with nothing pointing at what broke.

These are assumptions about the code's own correctness, not about
user input. Bad user input is already turned into an
AlzaraException upstream of both classes, so documenting them for
future maintainers, and failing loudly in development if they're
ever violated, calls for assert rather than another runtime check.

Let's add assert statements at each point. Bounds checks in
TaskList.get()/delete() and a non-null check in its constructor,
plus prefix checks in CommandParser.parseTodo/parseDeadline/
parseEvent immediately before the substring calls that depend on
them.

Placing each assert right where the assumption is relied on keeps
it next to the code it protects, and its failure message explains
which contract was broken and why it was expected to hold, rather
than leaving that to be inferred from a stack trace.

commitResults.messageTitle: Replace magic numbers with named constants in parser
commitResults.messageBody:
CommandParser's parseTodo/parseDeadline/parseEvent/parseKeywords
slice the command string using hardcoded offsets (5, 9, 6, 7) that
are really the lengths of literal keywords and markers - "todo ",
"deadline ", " /by ", "event ", " /from ", " /to ", "find " -
which already appear as separate literals in the same methods'
equals()/indexOf() calls.

An unexplained number next to a related literal is exactly the
"magic numbers" problem the SE-EDU code quality guide warns
against. If any of the literal keywords or markers is ever edited, the
matching offset silently goes stale and slices the wrong
substring.

Let's extract each keyword/marker into a named constant
(TODO_PREFIX, DEADLINE_PREFIX, EVENT_PREFIX, FIND_PREFIX,
BY_MARKER, FROM_MARKER, TO_MARKER) and replace every hardcoded
offset with that constant's length(), reusing the same constant
in the equals()/indexOf() calls that already needed it.

commitResults.messageTitle: Remove unused index parameter from Task.mark/unmark
commitResults.messageBody:
Task.mark(int index) and Task.unmark(int index) never use the
index. A reader sees task.mark(taskIndex) and reasonably assumes
the index matters when it is in fact silently ignored. This is the
"eliminate unused parameters" case the SE-EDU code quality guide
warns about under avoiding tripping up readers.

Let's drop the parameter from both methods and update every call
site to the no-arg form. ToDoTest's
mark_indexArgumentIgnored_taskMarkedDoneRegardless test is removed
too, since its entire premise - that the argument is ignored - no
longer applies once the argument doesn't exist.

commitResults.messageTitle: Replace magic numbers with named constants in Storage
commitResults.messageBody:
Storage.loadTask parses the save-file line "type | done | desc |
date..." using bare field-count checks (parts.length < 3/4/5) and
array indices (parts[0] through parts[4]). Nothing at each call
site says what "index 3" or "at least 4 fields" means - a reader
has to reverse-engineer that parts[3] is the date field, and that
the minimum-count checks are just "one more than the last index I
need." This is the same "Avoid Magic Numbers" case fixed in
CommandParser in an earlier commit.

Let's name each field's position (TYPE_INDEX, DONE_FLAG_INDEX,
DESCRIPTION_INDEX, DATE_INDEX, EVENT_END_DATE_INDEX) and derive
each minimum-field-count constant from the index it protects
(e.g. MIN_FIELD_COUNT_WITH_DATE = DATE_INDEX + 1) instead of
restating it as a separate literal, so the count can't drift out
of sync with the index behind it.

commitResults.messageTitle: Rename Task's task field/params to description
commitResults.messageBody:
Task's field holding a task's description is itself named task,
so inside a class called Task, a field called task reads as "a
task has a task" - it doesn't say what the value actually is. The
same task name is repeated in ToDo/Deadline/Event's constructor
parameters, even though every caller already refers to the same
value as description.

Let's rename the field and every constructor parameter that feeds
it - in Task, ToDo, Deadline, and Event - from task to
description, so the name matches what callers already call it and
says what it holds instead of just repeating the class name.

commitResults.messageTitle: Use streams in Task.matches and FindCommand.execute
commitResults.messageBody:
Task.matches loops over keywords, returning false on the first one
the description doesn't contain - exactly what Stream.allMatch
expresses directly, including the same short-circuit behaviour.
FindCommand.execute builds a list by looping and conditionally
adding - exactly what Stream.filter expresses directly.

Let's replace both loops with streams: Task.matches becomes
Arrays.stream(keywords).allMatch(...), and FindCommand.execute
becomes memory.getTasks().stream().filter(...).collect(...). Both
loops were doing textbook filter/allMatch work, so expressing them
as such states the intent directly instead of via loop mechanics
a reader has to trace through.
